quiz.question: Why does gender come out clustered on one side when a particular occupation is requested?
choices: Because a rule is written telling the model to judge that way
Because the distribution in the training material leans one way and the model reproduces that distribution
Because the request was too short
Because the image resolution was low
quiz.explanation: The model reproduces the distribution held in the material rather than making a judgment. Skew in the material comes out as skew in the result.

quiz.question: Why do results tilt toward the unobjectionable and resemble each other?
choices: Because the model stores the same answer
Because common high probability expressions are easier to select and preference tuning pushes the same way
Because the request is long
Because it passes through a translation step
quiz.explanation: In a structure that selects by probability, common expressions have the advantage, and human preference tuning makes what most raters liked the default.

quiz.question: How do you respond to bias in a recommendation list?
choices: Repeat the same question several times
Narrow the conditions by specifying region, period, or language
Ask for a longer list
Take the answer in English
quiz.explanation: Without narrowed conditions the list fills with frequently mentioned works. Specifying region, period, and scale produces a different list.

AI_ACADEMY_LESSONS.title: What People Must Decide When Using AI
AI_ACADEMY_LESSONS.description: AI can assist with production, but people must still define their taste, set the direction, and take responsibility for the result. Clear standards help determine what to delegate and what to verify yourself.
objectives: Explain why AI recommendations may differ from personal taste.
Identify why people must determine the direction of AI-assisted work.
Set review and approval procedures according to who is responsible for the result.

steps.title: How AI recommendations differ from personal taste
steps.contentMarkdown:
Ask AI to recommend a film and it will usually favor works that appear often in its sources and receive strong ratings from many people. As we saw earlier, its answers tend to lean toward aggregated judgments.

What many people like is not necessarily what you like. The two may overlap, but they do not always.

One person may find a scene dull while another notices something new in it. Even an acclaimed work can leave you cold. Taste develops from your experiences, the circumstances in which you encountered a work, and everything you had seen before it.

AI needs records to infer those influences. Give it your viewing history and reactions, and it can estimate your preferences from them. Without records, it has no basis for doing so.

To receive recommendations that reflect your taste, you need to record what you experienced and how it made you feel.

steps.title: Who determines the direction of the work
steps.contentMarkdown:
The person making something must choose the subject, decide what comes first, and determine what to leave out. Each choice changes the result.

Tasks such as organizing source material or drafting sentences can be delegated to AI. But if AI also sets the direction, the maker's judgment will not be visible in the finished work.

What to cut requires particular attention. Give AI a large collection of material and ask it to organize everything, and it may produce a result that includes it all. The maker must remove whatever does not serve the purpose. That standard comes from the production goal, not from the material itself.

The four-part request introduced earlier serves the same function. Before you can state the context and constraints, you must decide what result you want and what you will not allow. Writing a specific request means expressing those decisions clearly.

steps.title: Who is responsible for the result
steps.contentMarkdown:
Whoever releases an AI-assisted result cannot use the tool to avoid responsibility when something goes wrong. If a text includes a false claim, an image infringes someone else's rights, or a report contains a faulty judgment, responsibility rests with the person or organization that released it.

The standard can be stated in one question: **Who is responsible if it is wrong?** That party must define the review process and make the final decision.

In practice:

- The author checks facts against the original source.
- A responsible person approves any action that will be difficult to reverse.
- Before publication, the responsible person reviews the entire result again.
- The worker records which tools were used at each stage.

All four practices follow the same principle. The party responsible for the final result must identify errors and control whether the work proceeds.

steps.title: Why records of your taste matter
steps.contentMarkdown:
Keeping track of what you read, watch, and listen to helps you communicate your preferences more accurately when using AI.

**They provide evidence for estimating your taste.** Without personal records, recommendations will rely on the judgments of many other people. Your own notes show which works and passages you liked.

**They reveal how your taste has changed.** Compare what you wrote about a work five years ago with your response today, and you can see how your thinking has shifted. Only someone who kept the record can recover that information.

**They create standards for choosing new works.** As you note which subjects and forms of expression suit you, those patterns can guide your next choice.

The record does not need to be long. One or two lines about what you encountered and what stayed with you are enough. AI can summarize the whole work, but you should record the memorable part yourself. If someone else supplies that response, you cannot tell what actually moved you.

steps.title: What to know and how to judge
steps.contentMarkdown:
Using AI well requires an understanding of how it works, how to make requests, and how to evaluate its results.

First, we examined how AI produces an answer. Developers separate training from inference. AI divides sentences into tokens, uses attention to identify context, and appends the next token. Because of this process, it can also generate claims that are not true.

Next came the structure of a request. Fill in the four parts, provide examples, divide the work into steps, and add a verification procedure.

We then considered how images and sound are generated, copyright and other rights, the limits of detecting AI output, and the ways bias enters a result.

These principles help people decide how far to trust AI. That judgment determines what to do personally, what to delegate, and what to check at the end.

Specific standards also require knowledge of the field. To evaluate results, you need to understand light and composition in video, harmony in music, and classification and systems in books.

quiz.question: Why can taste not be delegated?
choices: Because the technology is not good enough yet
Because a majority rating differs from an individual's taste, and individual judgment comes out entangled with that person's experience
Because taste cannot be built from data, which makes recommendation itself impossible
Because computing taste takes too long
quiz.explanation: What a model returns is what is mentioned often and rated well by many. Individual judgment emerges from experience and situation, so it cannot be handled without your own records.

quiz.question: Which is least likely to be a decision a person has to make during production?
choices: Which subject to cover
What to put first
What to leave out
Transcription and caption timing
quiz.explanation: Choosing the subject, the arrangement, and what to discard creates the character of the result. Transcription and timing can be checked right away, which makes them good candidates for delegation.

quiz.question: Which assignment criterion recurred throughout this course?
choices: How much it costs
How long the work takes
Who answers for it when it is wrong
How long the output is
quiz.explanation: Fact checking, approval points, final review, and record keeping all come from this criterion. When responsibility lands on you, you hold the checking step yourself.
